pageCache.pageTitle: How Science Works Biology in Action
pageCache.text:
How Science Works Biology in Action
Year 12 students have been exploring how scientists turn observations into evidence through a hands-on Biology practical investigating the effect of temperature on maggot movement.
The experiment formed part of an introduction to “How Science Works”, giving students the opportunity to experience the scientific process rather than simply learning about it in theory.
Working at different temperatures, students observed the maggots and measured how far they travelled in one minute. By recording their results and comparing the distances, they were able to investigate whether changing the temperature affected the maggots’ activity.
The results showed a clear pattern: as the temperature increased, the maggots travelled further within the one-minute period.
As maggots are ectothermic, their body temperature and metabolic activity are influenced by the temperature of their surroundings. Within a suitable temperature range, warmer conditions can increase the rate of metabolic reactions and activity, helping to explain the increased movement observed during the experiment.
While the maggots may have been the focus of the experiment, the practical was really about developing the skills behind scientific investigation.
Students had to consider variables, accurate measurement, data collection, reliability and how evidence can be used to support a conclusion. They could also consider the limitations of their method and how repeating measurements or controlling other variables could make their findings more reliable.
It was an engaging introduction to practical Biology and an important reminder that science is not simply about knowing the answer — it is about asking questions, testing ideas and using evidence to understand the world around us.
Related news
Dr Sarah Watson | Principal
Oxford International College 1 London Place, Oxford OX4 1BD

PARENT ESSENTIALS
OUR SCHOOL CALENDAR
GOING ABOVE AND BEYOND
LIVING IN OXFORD
THE IMPORTANT INFORMATION YOU NEED
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQS)
Do students wear a uniform?
The college is a relaxed environment, and our students don’t wear a uniform. However, we do have a dress code. You’ll receive details about this in your pre-arrival pack.
Do you offer boarding?
Yes, boarding is an integral part of college life. Living in one of our four city-centre houses – which are just a short walk from our teaching buildings – our young people enjoy a genuine higher education-style experience. Students also receive 24/7 care and expert guidance from our experienced team of house parents. Find out more about boarding with us.
Which universities do your students go to?
Thanks to our comprehensive Global Strategic Pathways programme, our students receive offers from the world’s top-ranked universities. For the last two years, one in three applicants earned places to study medicine at either Oxford or Cambridge. What’s more, since 2019, more than half of our students have gone on to study at one of the UK’s prestigious G5 universities. Recent OIC graduates have been accepted by the University of Hong Kong, London School of Economics, and University of Toronto, among many others.
What nationalities are represented at the college?
Our culturally diverse college community is home to young people from more than 40 countries.
How do you support student health and wellbeing?
We know how important it is to help our young people settle into college life, both socially and academically. And that’s why, from their first day, we build a team around each student. This includes our dedicated pastoral department, boarding house parents, a mentor, and a progress tutor. We also employ a full-time nurse and a professional counsellor. Together, they look after every aspect of our learners’ growth and development.
THE LATEST NEWS AND EVENTS
Experts in their field, our teachers provide the specialist subject tuition and tailored guidance each student needs to achieve their goals.
Dr Sarah Watson | Principal
Oxford International College 1 London Place, Oxford OX4 1BD

COLLEGE CALENDAR
Please see below for our school year calendar, with the main term dates and holidays.
Term Dates 2026 - 2027
The academic year at OIC runs from early September to late June, although we do offer pre-sessional courses towards the end of August.
There are three terms each year: Autumn term, Spring term and Summer term. Each term has a half-term break and/or OIC Amplify Week activities.
Please note boarders may arrive upto a maximum of 2 days before the start of each term and must vacate one day after the College term ends. If you would like further information on these dates, please contact us at info@oxcoll.com
All dates are provisional and may be subject to minor changes.
Dr Sarah Watson | Principal
Oxford International College 1 London Place, Oxford OX4 1BD

JOBS AT OXFORD INTERNATIONAL COLLEGE (OIC)
TEACHING ROLES
Oxford International College (OIC) is a place of passion and purpose; a community where tutors and students inspire one another to be their very best.
Teaching here, you’ll work along some of the brightest minds in education. Our tutors are leaders in their fields who deliver a university-inspired model of teaching. Every day, you’ll innovate, push the boundaries, and challenge our students to go above and beyond. You’ll also provide the expert guidance and personalised support each individual needs to flourish.
In a diverse international community that’s focused on the future, we’ll support you to achieve your ambitions, too. What’s more, teaching and living in central Oxford offers a superb balance between work, education, and life.
HELPING YOU GROW
We encourage our tutors to expand their knowledge and share ideas with educators across the world. We encourage our staff to complete additional study to make sure they are always at the forefront of global educational trends.
We also offer great career development opportunities. Whatever your aims and aspirations, we’ll help you achieve them.
JOIN OUR TALENTED INDEPENDENT SCHOOL TEAM
Our pioneering approach to education delivers academic excellence, nurtures personal growth, and is designed around our students’ university and career aspirations.
Dr Sarah Watson | Principal
Oxford International College 1 London Place, Oxford OX4 1BD

INSPECTION REPORTS AND ACCREDITATIONS
OFSTED
Ofsted, the Office for Standards in Education, inspects schools across the UK to ensure they meet the government standards in both academics and boarding. This includes evaluating the quality of education and the care provided to boarding students, ensuring a safe and supportive environment for all learners.
ACCREDITATIONS, AFFILIATIONS AND RECOGNITION
The Boarding Schools’ Association (BSA) is the leading voice in education for boarding schools based in the UK and across the world. They represent member boarding schools, provides training for boarding staff and promotes boarding education. Their mission is to support excellence in boarding, safeguarding, inclusion and health education.
The Society of Heads is a welcoming, collegiate and supportive community of independent schools who evolve their approach to learning by sharing ideas and experiences. The overarching aim is to help provide appropriate and balanced curriculums within schools, which actively foster and develop key attributes in pupils.
The Independent Schools Council brings together seven associations of independent schools, their heads, bursars and governors. Through our member associations we represent over 1,400 independent schools in the UK and overseas.
AGBIS supports and advises governing bodies of schools in the independent sector on all aspects of governance, under the umbrella of the Independent Schools Council. The objectives of the Association are the advancement of education in independent schools and the promotion of good governance in such schools.
At Oxford International College, we accept applications all year round. We look forward to showing you around our campus and explaining how our ground-breaking educational approach will set you up for lifelong success.
Dr Sarah Watson | Principal
Oxford International College 1 London Place, Oxford OX4 1BD

UNIVERSITY ADMISSIONS EXPERTS
Future success doesn't happen by chance
At OIC, university preparation is built into the timetable, not added on.
From day one, students follow a structured programme that develops their ambitions, strengthens their academic profile and prepares them for the world's leading universities.
Supported by a dedicated University Pathway Advisor, every student receives personalised guidance throughout their journey, giving them the confidence to make informed choices and submit outstanding applications.
A DIFFERENT APPROACH
UNIVERSITY PREPARATION
Top universities look for more than strong results. They seek evidence of intellectual curiosity, resilience, leadership, and sustained subject engagement. This is preparation that goes deeper than the classroom - and gives families reassurance that progress is intentional, not accidental.
Strategic, high-impact portfolios
Authentic experience through competitions, projects, and internships
WHAT OUR SUPPORT INCLUDES
Specialist coaching for admissions tests, interviews and assessment centres helps students develop the confidence and skills needed to succeed at the world's most competitive universities.
UNIVERSITY OFFERS
EXPLORING PASSIONS
Every pathway produces a portfolio that proves both ability and ambition.
For students, this builds confidence.
Built in Oxford, we define futures through personalised academic pathways, world-class teaching, and a global perspective — that transform ambition into outstanding university offers and lifelong success.
Dr Sarah Watson | Principal
Oxford International College 1 London Place, Oxford OX4 1BD

Our Teachers
LEARNING FROM THE BEST
MEET OUR LEADERSHIP TEAM
Principal of Oxford International College, bringing 18 years’ international experience across schools in Oxford, London, Switzerland, Hong Kong and Halton. A research-informed leader, Dr Watson conducts and presents educational research nationally and internationally, combining academic rigour with compassionate, globally minded leadership.
Severine Collins is Vice Principal at Oxford International College and Designated Safeguarding Lead. She leads safeguarding, student and staff management with clarity, honesty and care, helping to create a safe, inclusive culture where people feel heard, protected and supported to succeed.
Ben Holman is Vice Principal, Pastoral at Oxford International College, bringing senior leadership experience across IB and UK schools in the UK, Colombia, Cambodia, Brazil and Peru. He is passionate about intercultural education, multilingual learners and creating inclusive environments where students thrive academically and personally.
Bringing more than 15 years’ experience across marketing, communications and education, with particular expertise in international student recruitment, brand strategy and admissions, Anna leads OIC’s marketing and recruitment strategy while ensuring families experience a personal and supportive journey from first enquiry to enrolment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 12 Begin Their University Pathways Journey
pageCache.text:
Year 12 Begin Their University Pathways Journey
Year 12 students came together for their first University Pathways session of the academic year, beginning the process of connecting their studies, wider academic interests and experiences with their future university ambitions.
Choosing a university course is about much more than deciding what to study after A Levels. At OIC, university preparation begins early, giving students time to explore their interests, understand what competitive universities are looking for and build a strong academic profile throughout Sixth Form.
During the session, Year 12 were introduced to OIC’s four Global Strategic Pathways: Clinical & Life Sciences, Physical & Applied Sciences, Computational & Data Sciences, and Social & Commerce Sciences.
Students explored the range of university subjects and careers connected to each pathway, from Medicine, Dentistry and Biochemistry to Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Economics, Law and PPE. The session encouraged them to think beyond individual degree titles and consider the wider fields, questions and challenges that genuinely interest them.
Students were also introduced to some of the people and resources that will support them throughout their university journey, including Dr Kirsten Dickers, Director of University Admissions & Careers, and Pathway Advisors Toby Blundell and William Goulder.
The session explored how UCAS and Unifrog can be used to research courses, universities, entry requirements and key application dates. Year 12 also looked ahead to the different elements that can form a competitive university application, including predicted grades, references and evidence of academic engagement beyond the classroom.
Importantly, students were encouraged to begin developing their wider knowledge from the very start of Year 12. Through carefully chosen electives and opportunities such as OIC Amplify and OIC Fusion, they can explore subjects in greater depth, undertake academic projects and begin building experiences relevant to their future ambitions.
Students were also introduced to SCITs – School-Centred Invigilated Tests – and the role that formative and summative assessment will play in demonstrating academic progress and informing predicted grades.
The session marked the beginning of a much longer process. Rather than waiting until Year 13 to think about university applications, Year 12 will begin working within their pathway groups, supported to make deliberate choices about their academic development, supercurricular activities and future direction.
With their pathways beginning to take shape, the focus now turns to exploring possibilities, developing academic depth and building the foundations for the university applications they will eventually make.
At OIC, university preparation starts from the moment students begin their Sixth Form journey.

SUPERCURRICULAR AND EXTRACURRICULAR ACTIVITIES
We help our students plan their personal and career development to support their academic goals.
Our unique supercurricular program ensures that every student develops personal experiences above and beyond the conventional syllabus.
SUPERCURRICULAR DEPARTMENT
Our Supercurricular Department delivers individualised 1:1 sessions and Career Meetings, where students are categorised and supported within groups of related academic disciplines. Our students do not only enter university applications with strong grades, but also a tangible appreciation and understanding of their future subject and career plans.
Beyond the syllabus
Programmes, awards and competitions
Clubs and societies
Further personal development
Considering university options
Applying to university
SUPERCURRICULAR V. EXTRACURRICULAR
The term “extracurricular” encompasses all activities students may do outside of the classroom – sports, charity work, or creative pursuits.
“Supercurricular” includes the career-centred acitivies. This could include attending degree-related guest lectures, work experience, or competitions.
OUR PROGRAMMES
Our Supercurricular Department ensures that all students are provided with hands-on experience through work shadowing and internships.
Please speak to our academic team to see how to enrol in the extra programmes.
Our Oxford Mentor Programme is designed to prepare students for their chosen career and to guide them through to successful university applications. The programme is delivered by mentors who are currently undergraduate, postgraduate or doctorate students at the University of Oxford. The programme consists of aptitude test preparation required to gain entry to certain degree courses and a bridging programme to widen students’ knowledge of their chosen career path in the fields of medicine, science, economics, engineering and law.
The programme is available to all OIC students and included in their tuition fees.
Each summer, students can also participate in the Goodwill Ambassador Programme in Malaysia which offers them the unique opportunity to get real-life exposure to their future degree subject by shadowing doctors, scientists, dentists, lawyers, engineers and other professionals.
After the first term, students are given the opportunity to take the Extended Project Qualification which gives them the opportunity to research a specific topic of interest beyond the A-level syllabus. The EPQ is highly recommended for students applying to top universities as it demonstrates a motivation to pursue further study in the student’s chosen subject and provides an impressive talking point in the personal statement and interviews.

Personal Pathway
Evidence shows the great importance that employers place on ‘character, attitude and behaviour’ in assessing the future potential of candidates. Similarly, university admissions tutors are looking not for what a student has already achieved, but what they are capable of achieving in the future.
This is particularly true of the elite universities like Oxbridge which receive only A*/A applicants, and so look for additional qualities in selecting the strongest candidates with the greatest potential.
Students are guided to take responsibility for their own performance and wellbeing through participation in enrichment and extra-curricular programmes that develop them as a person. Learning to be confident, resilient, pro-active and focussed is key to performing at our best. All students take part in an off-site residential course at the beginning of the academic year to introduce them to team-building and leadership skills and are encouraged to take part in the following activities throughout their stay with us.

To develop the same skillset, students are also encouraged to speak at weekly assemblies.
